title: Category Specialists: Filling a Need
brief: Which players are strong in one category (PTS, REB, AST, ST, BLK, 3PTM) and could fill a hole late in the auction or in season? It must warn that one-category players look better in punt rankings than they are and should not be bought to fix a category already lost.
summary: A one-category specialist helps only when the category is still winnable and his weak categories match the ones you already plan to punt. Punt rankings make these players look like top 100 options, but our league counts all nine categories every week. Never spend auction dollars or FAB on a specialist to rescue a category you have already lost.

paragraphs.text: A player who is elite in one category can look like a top 100 player in a ranking that punts his weak categories. That does not make him draftable in a standard league. Our league scores all nine categories every week. His holes count against you unless you have really given up those categories.

The same trap catches big men who are elite only in blocks, FG% and rebounds. Experts say these players get overdrafted in category leagues. Do not take them as early as round three, which is picks 25 to 36 in our 12-team league. In our auction, that means do not pay a third-round price for a three-category big.
Two more warnings. Do not let strong steals alone raise a player's value. A shooting guard who only makes threes and does not rebound or assist is a bad fantasy profile unless he is elite at threes.

Before you bid, read the player's full nine-category line, not his punt rank. List his weak categories. Then ask which of them your team already plans to give up. If the answer is none, he will cost you more than his ranking shows.

sections.heading: Do not buy back a lost category

paragraphs.text: Do not draft a one-category specialist to fix a category that is already too weak to recover. If your core buys leave you far behind in a category, treat it as a punt. Spend the dollars you have left on categories you can still win.

Many holes start early. Taking a two-category player early leaves holes in your team that you then have to fix. Before you pay a big price for a narrow player, count which categories he will leave empty and whether your later budget can cover them.

The same rule holds in season. We get at most 6 acquisitions per week and a limited FAB budget. Use them on a category you can swing in this week's matchup. Do not use them on a category you lose every week.

sections.heading: When filling a need is the right move

paragraphs.text: Track your category strengths and weaknesses during the draft. After each of your buys, note which of the nine categories you lead and which you lag. Pick to fill needs, for example a big man for rebounds or an early buy for assists.

Specialists fit best in the last of our 12 roster spots, after the 144-player pool has thinned. The right target is close to average in a category you are only a little behind in, and his weak categories are ones you already punt. A specialist whose weak spots hit categories you are trying to win is the wrong buy, even when he is cheap.

The experts disagree on how hard to chase a need. One side says you sometimes have to reach, taking a player a bit early just to get assists, and that a reach is fine if it fits your build because you need not be rigid about value. The other side says not to overindex on chasing a weak category like assists, and warns that buying narrow players early creates new holes. A workable middle ground: reach a little for a category that is still in play, and never reach for one already lost.

sections.heading: Checks before you bid or claim

paragraphs.text: Run four checks before every specialist bid on 2026-10-18 and every FAB claim after it. First, is the category still winnable? Second, do his weak categories match your punts? Third, is he elite in his one category, not just good? Fourth, would the price buy a third-round player? If it would, stop bidding.

Steals deserve one extra check. A player who brings steals and nothing else should not climb your list because of steals alone. Look for a second category he helps, or a punt that hides his weak spots.
